title: Encomiendas by the Lake
description: After the Spanish conquest of Manila, settlements around Laguna de Bay are distributed as encomiendas. The area of present-day San Pedro falls within the township of Tabuco.

title: Hacienda San Pedro de Tunasan
description: The Jesuit-run Colegio de San Jose consolidates its lands on the southwestern lakeshore into the Hacienda San Pedro de Tunasan, named for Saint Peter and the tunas plant that grew along the shore.

title: A Town of Its Own
description: By tradition, San Pedro de Tunasan is separated from Tabuco and becomes a town on January 18, 1725, with Francisco Santiago as its first mayor.

title: Revolution and Independence
description: San Pedro supports the revolution and shelters refugees from Cavite, including Gregoria de Jesus. Its municipal president, Gregorio Alvarez, joins the Bacoor Assembly that ratifies the Declaration of Independence.

title: Annexed to Biñan
description: Under Act No. 939 of the American colonial government, the town is dissolved and made part of Biñan.

title: Town Restored
description: Following Act No. 1553, the Municipality of San Pedro Tunasan is re-established, with Pascual Mindo as municipal president.

title: Renamed San Pedro
description: Act No. 2390 shortens the name of the town to San Pedro.

title: Liberation
description: After three years of Japanese occupation, guerrilla units liberate San Pedro on February 7, 1945.

title: The Hacienda Returns to the People
description: On August 30, 1954, President Ramon Magsaysay comes to the town plaza to witness the sale of the Hacienda San Pedro Tunasan to the government and signs the Agricultural Tenancy Act there. The land is later resold to its tenants and settlers.

title: First-Class Municipality
description: With industries and subdivisions growing through the postwar decades, San Pedro becomes a first-class municipality.

title: Cityhood
description: Republic Act No. 10420 converts San Pedro into a component city of Laguna. Residents ratify it in a plebiscite on December 28, 2013.

title: Twenty-Seven Barangays
description: Barangay San Vicente is divided into eight barangays, bringing the city to 27 barangays. Republic Act No. 11295 affirms the division in 2019.
